findings.claim: The mirror detection now depends on imported memories carrying a non-empty content_hash in memorycard. The promote_memorycard_test fixture had to be patched to set the hash on imported memories 2 and 4, which suggests imports may leave it empty. If a real imported memory has an empty hash, a hand-mirrored memory with the same text is no longer seen as holding the content of a paged observation. Promote and sync would then write a duplicate page where they previously refused it as bridged. MappedTwins also returns nothing for an empty hash, so this fails silently. I cannot confirm from the diff what real imports store.
proof_refs: longterm-mem/internal/memorycard/store.go MappedTwins: if contentHash == "" return nil
longterm-mem/cmd/longterm-mem/promote_memorycard_test.go: the test sets content_hash on memories 2 and 4 before the hand-mirrored check

findings.claim: toMemory now runs extra queries per memory: lineageOf, and mirrorsOf (MappedTwins plus one engramIDOf per twin). A listing over Candidates or Memories therefore issues N+1 queries on memorycard. This is probably cheap on a local SQLite file, but it is a cost the diff adds to sync of large projects.
proof_refs: longterm-mem/internal/memorycard/source.go toMemory calls s.lineageOf and s.mirrorsOf for each card
longterm-mem/internal/memorycard/store.go MappedTwins loops engramIDOf over the twins

evidence: I read only the diff; the implementations of MemoryIDsByEngramIDs and the Mapped field are not shown.
Removing the Engram handle from sync, promote and the MCP promote tool with source memorycard looks consistent: the imports and the unused variables were cleaned up.
The loss of hand-mirror detection when the twin has no imported memory is stated in the commit and covered by tests, so I did not count it as a defect.
